subject: Order form: multi-entity pricing ladder and invoice remittance path
messages:
From: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@nimblenet.io>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@nimblenet.io
Cc: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@nimblenet.io>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Initial: order form questions re: multi-entity billing and slab pricing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — Nimbus is excited to move forward. Our legal and finance teams reviewed the draft order form you shared. We have two topics that need clarity before procurement can issue an official PO:

1) Pricing ladder + minimum commit phasing: Nimbus will be migrating workloads across EU and US entities over Q4. We need to confirm how the pricing slabs will apply if usage is split across two invoice entities in the same quarter. Specifically: can slabs/thresholds be aggregated for the customer (single consumption across entities) or do you require per-entity slabs?

2) Invoice remittance path & tax evidence: Our AP team requires a clear remit-to entity on the order form and will need Redwood's VAT registration certificate and suggested tax-residency evidence. Attached is our PO template (Nimbus_PO_template.xml) for your ops team to review.

Can you loop in finance and confirm what the invoicing options are (single invoice to Nimbus EU entity vs split invoices per entity) and the impact on minimum commitments / pricing tiers?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our commercial window is tight.

Best,
Lena
Procurement Manager
Nimbus Systems

[Attachment: Nimbus_PO_template.xml (attachment stub)]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@nimblenet.io>, procurement@nimblenet.io
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Initial: order form questions re: multi-entity billing and slab pricing

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (finance) and Ben (sales ops) to confirm options. Quick answers up-front: we support both single consolidated billing and split-entity invoicing, but the treatment of minimum commits and slab aggregation differs and may affect effective unit price. Details below and a suggested approach so you can share with AP/legal.

A) Pricing slab aggregation
- Option 1 — Consolidated consumption: We can aggregate usage across entities for pricing/thresholds if Nimbus provides an entity-level allocation schedule in the order form (i.e., which invoices map to which legal entity) and signs a single commercial commitment on behalf of the group. This requires an amendment to the order form that lists the consolidation clause.
- Option 2 — Per-entity billing: If you want separate legal contracts/invoices per entity, slabs/thresholds are evaluated per invoice entity. That typically increases the blended unit cost versus consolidated aggregation.

B) Minimum commit phasing
- For migrations across entities we can stagger the minimum commit: 60% in Q4 (EU entity) + 40% in Q1 (US entity) as a simple example. We need the exact phasing and dates in the order form appendix so billing ops can map commits to invoices.

C) Invoice remit & tax evidence
- Redwood prefers the remit-to to match the invoiced legal entity exactly for VAT/regulatory reasons. If you want a single invoice routed to your EU AP team while the legal buyer is a US entity, we will need written evidence of tax residency and a billing agent arrangement.

Attachments requested: please share Nimbus VAT certificate and the signed remit instructions. We've attached an editable order form appendix template (redwood_orderform_draft.pdf) with fields for entity mapping and commit phasing.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Nimbus confirms desired billing model (consolidated vs per-entity) and provides VAT docs.
2) Redwood drafts an order form appendix capturing entity mapping and commit phasing for legal to review (we can do a clean redline).
3) Finance to confirm any change to net terms (net30 default; net45 considered for multi-entity).

Kimberly / Ben — can you confirm if net45 is an option here and whether split invoicing adds operational overhead requiring cadence changes?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_orderform_draft.pdf (attachment stub)]

From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@nimblenet.io>, procurement@nimblenet.io
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: order form questions re: multi-entity billing and slab pricing

Thanks Karthik / Lena — finance here. Short answers and the ops-level asks so AP can process invoices cleanly.

1) Net terms
- We can offer Net45 on this deal (deal id DF-47821) provided we receive a single-parent commercial commitment (consolidated billing) or a cross-company guarantee if you insist on per-entity legal buyers. Net30 remains our standard for split-entity invoicing.

2) Tax evidence / remit flow
- If you select consolidated billing but want the invoice physically routed to Nimbus EU AP, we require: (a) VAT registration for the billed entity; (b) a signed billing agent letter that authorizes the receiving AP to pay on behalf of the billed entity; (c) a completed tax residency form.

3) Practical ops notes
- Split invoices: expect per-month separate invoices per entity (two PDFs), separate remittance advices, and distinct account codes. This increases AP reconciliation time and may delay early payment discounts.
- Consolidated: single invoice; we will map consumption internally and provide entity-level breakdowns in the invoice detail CSV.

Requested items from Nimbus to finalize orderform appendix:
- Confirm billing model (consolidated vs per-entity).
- Provide VAT cert(s) and the completed tax residency form.
- If consolidated, provide a signed consolidation clause (we can draft).

I can prepare a concise appendix for legal once you confirm the above. If you'd like, we can also schedule a 30-minute call to walk AP through the remit flow and sample invoice layout.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Finance Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

[No attachment]

From: Martin Lopez <martin.lopez@nimblenet.io>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: Lena Hoffman <lena.hoffman@nimblenet.io>, procurement@nimblenet.io
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: order form questions re: multi-entity billing and slab pricing

Karthik / Kimberly — thanks for the clarity. Nimbus prefers consolidated billing for pricing efficiency but requires the physical invoice to be sent to our EU AP mailbox (ap.eu@nimblenet.io). We are prepared to sign a consolidation clause and provide the VAT certificate (attached: Nimbus_tax_certificate.pdf).

Requests before we sign:
- Please send the draft consolidation clause and the appendix with exact commit phasing so our legal can run a quick review.
- Can Redwood confirm that a single invoice routed to EU AP will still allow us to claim group-level slab aggregation for pricing? We understand billing ops will provide an entity-level CSV breakdown — that is acceptable.

We attached our signed PO with minor comments on the remit-to field; comments are inline in the redwood_orderform_draft.pdf. If everything else looks good we can push to signature by EOW.

Thanks,
Martin Lopez
Head of Finance, Nimbus Systems

[Attachments: Nimbus_tax_certificate.pdf, signed_redwood_orderform_comments.pdf (inline comments)]
